newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW -- Western says to sell Tyco shrs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW -- Western says to sell Tyco shrs.

text.p: Western Resources Inc chairman John Hayes said the company intends to sell its 13.5 million Tyco International Ltd shares "as soon as we can do so on an orderly basis."

"We have an arrangement with Tyco for an orderly exit," Hayes said in an interview with Reuters, adding Tyco has indicated a willingness to participate in a "road show" to promote the sale of the shares, if the companies so choose.
Western came to hold a large Tyco position through the ownership of equity in ADT Ltd, which was acquired by Tyco, effective July 2.
Western's ADT position converted into about 18.4 million Tyco shares.
Western has sold five million Tyco shares for $387 million. It now holds about 13.5 million shares of Tyco currently valued at about $1.1 billion, based on Tyco's share price as of July 28.
Western's original investment cost about $590 million.
Earlier Wednesday, Western announced a $320 million deal to acquire 80.1 percent of Protection One Inc and the transfer of its security assets to the company.

The deal is expected to close this fall, pending Protection One shareholder approval, and would create the second largest monitored security company in the United States, behind Tyco's top spot arrived at with the ADT deal.

Of the $320 million, $250 million in cash would go to pay down Protection One debt and $117 million in cash would be used for a one-time $7 a share dividend to existing Protection One shareholders, Hayes said in a telephone interview.
Protection One also will assume "$47 million in obligations associated with our recent Westinghouse (Security Systems) trasnsction," Hayes said.
Last December, Western announced the acquisition of Westinghouse Electric Corp's monitored security services business for about $470 million.

In explaining the structure of the Protection One transaction, Hayes said, "It gives us the opportunity to establish a market multiple for our security interests" separate from Western's primary business of electric and gas utilities.
Almost 20 percent of Protection One's outstanding shares will continue to be publicly traded on Nasdaq, Hayes said.
Western is based on Topeka, Kan., and Protection One's headquarters is in Culver City, Calif.

In a media conference call after the interview, Western's chief financial officer Steven Kitchen said the Protection One transaction is expected to be dilutive to Western earnings in the first two years after closure and accretive in the third year.
The magnitude of both the initial diliution and subsequent accretion is expected to be in the single-digit percentage range, the CFO said in response to a question.
According to First Call, Wall Street's 1997 consensus earnings expectation for Western is $2.64 per share.
